newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco to absorb Spanish bank.
newsitem.headline: Morocco to absorb Spanish bank.

text.p: Morocco's leading Wafabank is to buy 100 percent of the Spanish Uniban bank, Wafabank president Abdelhak Bennani said on Thursday.
"The decision of purchase was taken after a meeting of the board of directors on Tuesday," Bennani told Reuters.
Final agreement will be sealed when Uniban's general assembly meets on December 30, 1996 and after approval by the monetary authorities, Bennani said.
The Spanish bank has a capital of 246 million dirhams ($28 million) or a total of 2.4 million shares.
The bank registered a net profit of 0.6 million dirhams in the first half of this year from losses of 27.2 million dirhams in the whole period of 1995.
"The effective absorption of Uniban will take place in the first quarter of 1997 after an exchange of one share of Wafabank against five shares of Uniban," Bennani said.
Wafabank aims to diversify its financial sources and take a larger stake on the market, including opening a branch in Madrid. It also targets reduction of its costs in future, he added.

With a market capitalisation of 2.9 billion dirhams and one of the market's most liquid stocks, Wafabank made a net profit of 83 million dirhams in the first half of the year from 78.4 million in the same period in 1995.
Wafabank's turnover reached 801.5 million dirhams for the period of January-June 1996 from 711 million dirhams in the same period last year.
Fuelled by the rumours of the merger, Wafabank shares were in demand on the stock exchange and rose over the line of 500 dirhams in recent weeks.
Reacting to the news, its share value jumped 12 dirhams to close at 535 dirhams on Thursday.
Established in Casablanca since 1911, Wafabank is among the 47 stocks listed on the 67-year-old Casablanca stock exchange.
